From 7eb7ae283557d8467403b9db35605861a0870add Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Christopher Faulet <cfaulet@haproxy.com>
Date: Fri, 5 Jan 2024 16:48:40 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] BUG/MEDIUM: stconn: Forward shutdown on write timeout only if
 it is forwardable

The commit b9c87f8082 ("BUG/MEDIUM: stconn/stream: Forward shutdown on write
timeout") introduced a regression. In sc_cond_forward_shut(), the write
timeout is considered too early to forward the shutdown. In fact, it is
always considered, even if the shutdown is not forwardable yet. It is of
course unexpected. It is especially an issue when a write timeout is
encountered on server side during the connection establishment. In this
case, if shutdown is forwarded too early on the client side, the connection
is closed before the 503 error sending.

So the write timeout must indeed be considered to forward the shutdown to
the underlying layer, but only if the shutdown is forwardable. Otherwise, we
should do nothing.

This patch should fix the issue #2404. It must be backported as far as 2.2.

diff --git a/src/stconn.c b/src/stconn.c
index b3aed9521..74efca7ef 100644
--- a/src/stconn.c
+++ b/src/stconn.c
@@ -522,15 +522,11 @@ struct appctx *sc_applet_create(struct stconn *sc, struct applet *app)
  */
 static inline int sc_cond_forward_shut(struct stconn *sc)
 {
-	/* Forward the shutdown if an write error occurred on the input channel */
-	if (sc_ic(sc)->flags & CF_WRITE_TIMEOUT)
-		return 1;
-
 	/* The close must not be forwarded */
 	if (!(sc->flags & (SC_FL_EOS|SC_FL_ABRT_DONE)) || !(sc->flags & SC_FL_NOHALF))
 		return 0;
 
-	if (co_data(sc_ic(sc))) {
+	if (co_data(sc_ic(sc)) && !(sc_ic(sc)->flags & CF_WRITE_TIMEOUT)) {
 		/* the shutdown cannot be forwarded now because
 		 * we should flush outgoing data first. But instruct the output
 		 * channel it should be done ASAP.
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

**File: `src/stconn.c`**
- The code that previously forwarded the shutdown on a write timeout has been removed. Specifically, the check for `CF_WRITE_TIMEOUT` that returned `1` (indicating shutdown forwarding) has been eliminated.
- A new condition has been added to ensure that shutdown forwarding only occurs if the shutdown is forwardable, which is determined by checking that the input channel does not have the `CF_WRITE_TIMEOUT` flag set. This change prevents premature shutdown forwarding when a write timeout occurs.

### Relationships Between Modifications
The modifications in `src/stconn.c` address a regression introduced by a previous commit. The change ensures that shutdown forwarding on write timeouts is contingent upon the shutdown being forwardable. This relationship is crucial as it prevents the connection from being closed prematurely during critical operations, such as connection establishment, thereby resolving the issue identified in bug report #2404. The patch effectively refines the logic for handling write timeouts to enhance the stability and correctness of the connection management process.

BUG/MEDIUM: stconn: Forward shutdown on write timeout only if
 it is forwardable

The commit b9c87f8082 ("BUG/MEDIUM: stconn/stream: Forward shutdown on write
timeout") introduced a regression. In sc_cond_forward_shut(), the write
timeout is considered too early to forward the shutdown. In fact, it is
always considered, even if the shutdown is not forwardable yet. It is of
course unexpected. It is especially an issue when a write timeout is
encountered on server side during the connection establishment. In this
case, if shutdown is forwarded too early on the client side, the connection
is closed before the 503 error sending.

So the write timeout must indeed be considered to forward the shutdown to
the underlying layer, but only if the shutdown is forwardable. Otherwise, we
should do nothing.

This patch should fix the issue #2404. It must be backported as far as 2.2.

Here is the root cause:
The bug was caused by the premature forwarding of shutdown signals on write timeouts, which occurred even when the shutdown was not forwardable. This led to connections being closed before errors could be properly communicated, particularly during connection establishment on the server side.

Here is the patch:
  */
 static inline int sc_cond_forward_shut(struct stconn *sc)
 {
-	/* Forward the shutdown if an write error occurred on the input channel */
-	if (sc_ic(sc)->flags & CF_WRITE_TIMEOUT)
-		return 1;
-
 	/* The close must not be forwarded */
 	if (!(sc->flags & (SC_FL_EOS|SC_FL_ABRT_DONE)) || !(sc->flags & SC_FL_NOHALF))
 		return 0;
 
-	if (co_data(sc_ic(sc))) {
+	if (co_data(sc_ic(sc)) && !(sc_ic(sc)->flags & CF_WRITE_TIMEOUT)) {
 		/* the shutdown cannot be forwarded now because
 		 * we should flush outgoing data first. But instruct the output
 		 * channel it should be done ASAP.
 		 */
 		sc_schedule_shutdown(sc);
 		return 0;
 	}
 
 	/* the close can be immediately forwarded to the write side */
 	return 1;
 }
